children.text: The TikTok that I'll be analyzing comes from Brian Johnson, known online as Liver King, a fitness and wellness influencer on TikTok and Instagram whose entire persona rests on the claim that he lives an "ancestral" lifestyle, eating raw organ meat, rejecting modern conveniences, and attributing his extreme physique to primal habits alone. That persona is also his business, since nearly every video, including the one I am analyzing, exists to sell his "Ancestral Supplements" line, meaning his authenticity is not just a personality trait but the product itself. What connects him to our group's theme of influencer controversy is that his fame was never built on quiet consistency, it was built on being extreme enough to argue about, and in late 2022, leaked emails revealed that his physique came from steroid use rather than diet, prompting him to publicly admit "I lied" after months of denial. That confession set off a wave of mainstream press coverage, mockery, and a fraud lawsuit from customers who bought his supplements believing his ancestral claims, and rather than disappearing, Liver King became more widely known after the scandal than before it. His career shows how controversy can work in an influencer's favor even when it exposes them as dishonest, since the attention generated by the "I lied" scandal circulated his name and his brand far past his original fitness-niche audience, proving the same "all publicity is good publicity" logic our group identified.
